label: Structured shared-IO feature process - all latent widths 1024 - rank-256 trainable low-rank GNGLU maps - original production-basis dense nonzero-target dataset - K1 2x1s input x 59 - K2 2x1s output x 59 - standardized next-feature MSE - 256k clean - batch 10240 train and evaluation - no regularization - weight EMA 4 epochs

linearFactorization.scope: projection, value transform, gate transform, and output map in every numbered and unnumbered GNGLU block
linearFactorization.rankCeiling: each matrix uses min(256,input width,output width), so the 59-wide IO boundaries retain their complete attainable rank without redundant factors
linearFactorization.identityBase: value/gate transforms and rectangular output maps use fixed identity bases plus trainable low-rank residuals

architecture.numberedLayerSharing: each parenthesized number in the diagram is one exact GNGLU module instance reused at every matching input/output block
architecture.initialState: the first observed W embedding seeds M and P with two unnumbered GNGLUs; shared layer 3 produces F and shared layer 4 produces PF
architecture.outputState: shared layer 7 maps PF to NF; shared layer 8 maps NF to expected W; shared layer 2 decodes W to the complete next-second O-feature state
architecture.latentSemantics: P, F, PF, and NF remain unconstrained latent embeddings in this experiment; no probability decoder or density loss is imposed

loss.description: mean MSE over both predicted output steps and all 59 feature channels after per-feature training-split standardization

sampling.description: original dense chronological clean-origin dataset with exact-zero next-return targets excluded
sampling.comparisonControl: same K1/K2, optimizer, loss, examples, batches, and EMA as the all-512 predecessor; every latent width doubles to 1024 while all GNGLU matrices use trainable rank-256 factorization

evaluation.headline: step-1 next completed 1s signed log return

alignment.input: two consecutive timeline rows ending at each clean example origin
alignment.target: the two complete chronological timeline rows at origin+1 and origin+2
alignment.futureExtension: K1 uses consecutive rows ending at origin; K2 uses consecutive rows starting at origin+1
